source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: What is the DOH standard procedure for bilateral tubal ligation?
questions.rationale: Minilaparotomy under local anesthesia with light sedation is the DOH standard; general anesthesia is the greatest risk.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 10 BTL (PDF p. 204)
questions.quote: BTL by minilaparotomy under local anesthesia is the accepted standard procedure of the Department of Health

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A mother delivered 2 weeks ago and requests BTL. The nurse explains it should be done:
questions.rationale: BTL can be done within 7 days of birth or after 6 weeks; it is delayed from 7 to 42 days postpartum.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 10 Timing of BTL (PDF p. 209)
questions.quote: except between seven days and six weeks after childbirth

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Before minilaparotomy BTL, the client is told to:
questions.rationale: No solid food for at least 6 hours; clear fluids are allowed up to 2 hours before surgery.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 10 Before the procedure (PDF p. 210)
questions.quote: Not eat any solid food for at least six hours before surgery

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: After BTL, when may the client be discharged?
questions.rationale: Observe at least 2 hours; discharge when vital signs are stable and she tolerates food.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 10 After the procedure (PDF p. 211)
questions.quote: Discharge the client when her vital signs are stable and when she can tolerate food intake.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which sign after BTL needs immediate referral?
questions.rationale: High fever (>38 °C) in the first 4 weeks, pus, worsening pain or fainting need referral.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 10 Complications (PDF p. 212)
questions.quote: High fever (> 38 °C) in the first four weeks

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which is one of the six elements of informed consent for sterilization?
options: She may decide against it anytime
It must be done after age 35
questions.rationale: The client can withdraw before the operation without losing other services; it is permanent and gives no STI protection.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 10 Informed consent (PDF p. 213)
questions.quote: The client can decide against the procedure at any time before the operation is performed

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which client is most likely to regret sterilization later?
questions.rationale: Regret is more likely in those who are young, have few or no children, or have marital problems.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 10 Counseling (PDF p. 213)
questions.quote: Have few or no children

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A married woman wants postpartum tubal ligation. Whose consent is required?
questions.rationale: Only the client's (not the husband's) consent is required; involving the spouse in counseling may help.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 11 Postpartum women (PDF p. 241)
questions.quote: Only the client's (not the husband's) consent is required to perform this procedure.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A clinic offers BTL only to women over 35 with 3 children. This policy is:
questions.rationale: Sterilization must not be limited by age or number of children; each person decides.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 10 Counseling (PDF p. 213)
questions.quote: Sterilization should not be offered only to women who have had a certain number of children or who have reached a certain age.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Why is no-scalpel vasectomy preferred?
questions.rationale: NSV uses a puncture, with less pain and tissue trauma and shorter operating and recovery time.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 10 Vasectomy (PDF p. 216)
questions.quote: less pain and tissue trauma and shorter operating and recovery time

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A man asks when his vasectomy becomes fully effective. The nurse says:
questions.rationale: Clearing live sperm from the tract takes 3 months; use condoms until then.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 10 Vasectomy effectiveness (PDF p. 217)
questions.quote: full effectiveness can only be achieved three months after the procedure

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which post-vasectomy instruction is correct?
questions.rationale: Tight-fitting underwear relieves pain and swelling; rest 2 days and keep the wound dry.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 10 After the procedure (PDF p. 222)
questions.quote: Wear tight fitting underwear or pants to relieve some pain, swelling, or bleeding.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A man worries vasectomy will weaken his erections. The nurse explains that vasectomy:
questions.rationale: Vasectomy does not affect hormones, erection or ejaculation; only sperm is absent from semen.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 10 Vasectomy advantages (PDF p. 218)
questions.quote: Does not affect male hormonal function, erection, and ejaculation

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: What is a common complication to watch for after vasectomy?
questions.rationale: Hematoma is common, so bleeding is checked carefully; vasectomy does not raise cancer risk.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 10 NSV procedure (PDF p. 221)
questions.quote: Meticulously check for bleeding because hematoma formation is a common complication.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: If both partners accept permanent methods, which is preferred and why?
questions.rationale: Vasectomy is simpler, safer, easier and less costly than female sterilization.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 10 Vasectomy FAQs (PDF p. 227)
questions.quote: vasectomy would be preferable because it is simpler, safer, easier, and less expensive than female sterilization

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: A sexually active 17-year-old asks for contraception. Which approach is correct?
questions.rationale: Adolescents need confidential, non-judgmental counseling; all modern reversible methods are safe; sterilization is avoided.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 11 Adolescents (PDF p. 230)
questions.quote: young individuals must be assured of confidentiality and privacy

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Why do adolescents often stop using contraceptives?
questions.rationale: High discontinuation is due to low tolerance of side effects; counsel that effects are temporary.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 11 Adolescents (PDF p. 230)
questions.quote: High discontinuation rates in this age group are due to low threshold to tolerance to some side effects.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A 38-year-old smokes 20 cigarettes daily. Which method is unacceptable for her?
questions.rationale: Women over 35 smoking 15 or more daily: all combined hormonal methods are MEC 4.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 11 Smokers (PDF p. 238)
questions.quote: If a woman smokes at least 15 sticks a day, then all four of these methods are unacceptable (MEC 4)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: An obese woman uses Implanon. When should she return for replacement?
questions.rationale: Etonogestrel levels fall with body weight; obese users return after 2 years (Jadelle users over 60 kg after 4).
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 11 Women with obesity (PDF p. 234)
questions.quote: Obese etonogestrel implant (Implanon) users should also be advised to return after two years

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: When can a non-breastfeeding mother start combined pills after birth?
questions.rationale: Non-breastfeeding women can start COCs at 3 weeks; breastfeeding women wait until 6 months.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 11 Postpartum women (PDF p. 245)
questions.quote: COCs can be initiated three weeks after birth.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Why is family planning started early in a non-breastfeeding mother?
options: Fertility is low for a year
questions.rationale: Ovulation may resume about 25 days after birth in non-breastfeeding women.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 11 Postpartum women (PDF p. 239)
questions.quote: ovulation may resume approximately 25 days after she has given birth

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A 50-year-old with a copper IUD had her last period 4 months ago. The nurse advises:
questions.rationale: FP is continued for 1 year after the last menses; the copper IUD is removed 12 months after the LMP.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 11 Perimenopause (PDF p. 248)
questions.quote: the device is removed 12 months after the last menstrual period
